ai.definition: RAG Pipelines for Enhanced Knowledge Retrieval is a technology that integrates retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) models to enhance the accuracy and contextual relevance of information retrieval and content generation tasks.
ai.howItWorks: This technology combines retrieval-based models, which search existing knowledge bases or databases for relevant information, with generative models, which create new text based on learned patterns. By first retrieving contextually relevant snippets from a database and then using these as input to a generative model, RAG pipelines can produce more accurate and coherent responses.
ai.problemSolved: Traditional retrieval systems often struggle to provide contextually rich or semantically accurate information, while generative models alone may lack factual accuracy. RAG pipelines address this by leveraging the strengths of both approaches.
ai.manufacturing: The manufacturing process involves developing and training both retrieval-based and generative models, integrating them into a pipeline architecture, and fine-tuning the system to optimize performance across various use cases.
ai.buildProcess: Building an RAG pipeline requires extensive data preprocessing, model selection, parameter tuning, and iterative testing. The process is highly dependent on the quality and relevance of the training data.
ai.costDrivers: Key cost drivers include the acquisition and processing of high-quality training data, computational resources for model training and inference, and ongoing maintenance costs to keep models updated with new information.
ai.lifecycleOutlook: The outlook is promising as the technology continues to evolve and gain traction in various applications. However, it remains in an early stage of development and commercialization.
ai.regulation: Currently, there are no specific regulations targeting RAG pipelines, but general data privacy laws and ethical guidelines for AI may apply depending on the use case.
ai.risks: Risks include potential biases in training data, difficulty in ensuring factual accuracy, and challenges in maintaining model performance over time as new information becomes available.
ai.profitability: Profitability is uncertain at this stage due to the early development phase and limited commercial applications. However, successful implementation could lead to significant cost savings and improved efficiency in knowledge management tasks.
ai.futureDevelopment: Future developments may focus on improving model accuracy, expanding use cases, and addressing ethical concerns related to bias and transparency.

glossary.def: A technology that combines retrieval-based and generative models for more accurate information retrieval and content generation.
A method where a retrieval model first finds relevant context from a knowledge base, which is then used as input to a generative model to produce coherent responses.

subsystems.name: Ingestion and parsing
subsystems.role: turns source documents into clean text plus metadata.
parts: connectors to file stores, wikis and databases
format parsers for PDF, HTML and office files
text extractors for tables and images

subsystems.name: Chunking
subsystems.role: splits documents into passages small enough to embed and retrieve.
parts: splitter by headings, sentences or token count

subsystems.name: Embedding model
subsystems.role: converts each chunk into a vector that encodes meaning.

subsystems.name: Index and retriever
subsystems.role: finds the chunks closest to a query, fast.
parts: vector index using approximate nearest-neighbour search
keyword index (e.g. BM25) for exact terms

subsystems.name: Reranker
subsystems.role: re-scores the shortlist so the most relevant passages reach the model.

subsystems.name: Generator and prompt assembly
subsystems.role: writes the answer using only the retrieved context, with citations.

subsystems.name: Evaluation and monitoring
subsystems.role: measures whether retrieval and answers are actually correct, and catches drift.

buildSteps.title: Collect the corpus
buildSteps.detail: Decide which documents the system may use, pull them through connectors, and record permissions so users only retrieve what they are allowed to see.

buildSteps.title: Parse and clean
buildSteps.detail: Extract text, strip boilerplate such as navigation and headers, and preserve tables and headings as structured metadata.

buildSteps.title: Chunk the text
buildSteps.detail: Split into passages of a few hundred tokens along natural boundaries, with slight overlap so no sentence is cut in half.

buildSteps.title: Embed and index
buildSteps.detail: Run each chunk through the embedding model and write the vectors, plus the raw text and metadata, into a vector index; build the keyword index alongside.

buildSteps.title: Retrieve
buildSteps.detail: At query time, embed the question, run vector and keyword searches in parallel, and merge the two ranked lists.

buildSteps.title: Rerank and filter
buildSteps.detail: Score the shortlisted passages with a cross-encoder, drop weak or stale ones, and enforce access rules.

buildSteps.title: Assemble the prompt
buildSteps.detail: Fit the best passages into the model's context window, numbered and labelled, with an instruction to answer only from them.

buildSteps.title: Generate with citations
buildSteps.detail: The model writes the answer and points each claim back to a passage; if the context is insufficient it should say so instead of guessing.

buildSteps.title: Evaluate and iterate
buildSteps.detail: Run a fixed question set after every change, measuring retrieval hit rate and answer faithfulness, and log real queries to find gaps.

prerequisites.why: the generator must follow instructions and synthesise fluent text from supplied context.
retrieval depends on mapping questions and passages into the same semantic vector space.
exact comparison against millions of vectors would be far too slow.
bigger windows let more passages fit, but recall still degrades in the middle of very long inputs.
without measurement it is hard to tell a well-sourced answer from a plausible invention.

pathway.milestone: hybrid vector plus keyword search with a reranker and citation output
pathway.unlocks: useful question answering over private document sets.

pathway.milestone: agentic retrieval that rewrites the query, retrieves in several steps and calls tools
pathway.unlocks: answers to multi-part questions that a single lookup cannot serve.

pathway.milestone: graph and structure-aware retrieval over linked entities
pathway.unlocks: reasoning across relationships rather than isolated passages.

pathway.milestone: continuously updated indexes with automatic freshness, permission and quality checks
pathway.unlocks: knowledge systems that stay correct as the underlying documents change.
